title: Paloma and the Wolf
premise: Astrid Hartwell, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers who once served the old gods, has survived thirty years by smuggling goods through the Thornfell mountains and pretending the gods are dead. But when prayers begin to be answered again—first in small ways, then in terrifying ones—the usurper King Veyric launches a purge to find and destroy whatever is waking. Astrid discovers they carry the last living fragment of the god Ondrys sealed in their own blood, a secret their dying mentor hid from them. Hunted by Veyric's witch-finders and courted by desperate free-city envoys, Astrid must choose between remaining invisible or becoming the weapon that either reignites the ancient war between gods and mortals—or ends it for good. In the end, Astrid refuses both war and godhood, shattering Ondrys's fragment so no one can wield it, and finds belonging not in divine purpose but among the ragged found-family who chose to stand with them.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is the pen name of a former mountain guide who grew up in a Norwegian immigrant family in the Pacific Northwest, where winter stories were currency. Their fiction blends Norse-inflected myth with quiet, character-driven fantasy about outsiders finding their people.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Smuggling salt and secrets through Thornfell, Astrid notices the mountain paths shifting to favor them—old magic behaving strangely. They dismiss it as weather and superstition. Emotional beat: weary competence masking deep loneliness; the reader senses the world is already changing around them.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: In the border town of Lowmark, Astrid witnesses a dying child healed when her mother prays at a cracked roadside shrine. The crowd's terror and awe ripple outward. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder—the gods returning is not good news for someone hiding from them.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: King Veyric declares all shrines to the old gods forfeit and dispatches his witch-finders. Free-city envoy Sela Voss arrives in Lowmark seeking a guide through Thornfell—and recognizes Astrid's surname from old oaths. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: cornered; invisibility is ending whether they like it or not.

chapters.title: What the Mentor Buried
chapters.summary: Astrid returns to their hidden cabin and finds their dying mentor, Halvard, waiting with a confession: the swordspeaker oaths never died—they sleep in bloodlines, and Astrid carries something more. He dies before explaining fully. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: grief braided with betrayal; the secret becomes personal.

chapters.title: Blood in the Snow
chapters.summary: Pursued by witch-finder Captain Dreven, Astrid's blood spilled on an ancient waystone wakes a guardian spirit that slaughters their attackers. Astrid flees, horrified by what they can call. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: fear of self; power revealed as something monstrous before it is anything else.

chapters.title: Sela's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sela catches up to Astrid and offers protection and purpose: the free cities need a swordspeaker to rally resistance against Veyric. Astrid refuses, but agrees to guide her—for a price. Alternating POV begins with Sela. Emotional beat: wary negotiation; two survivors sizing each other up.

chapters.title: The Hollow Shrine
chapters.summary: Deep in Thornfell, the party shelters in a ruined temple where Astrid hears Ondrys's voice for the first time—a god's whisper inside their own skull, patient and hungry. Sela's POV reveals she suspects what Astrid is and is already calculating. Emotional beat: violation; even sanctuary is occupied territory now.

chapters.title: Veyric's Court
chapters.summary: King Veyric's POV chapter. We see his genuine terror of the returning gods and how it curdles into fanaticism—he burned his own brother as a vessel years ago. He orders Thornfell sealed and every Hartwell descendant found. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy; the villain believes he is the shield.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Astrid and Sela gather fellow travelers: Tam, a defected witch-finder scribe; Yara, a shrine-keeper's daughter who hears the gods clearly; and Brannic, a disgraced free-city soldier. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: tentative warmth; the found-family assembles around a fire, and Astrid almost belongs.

chapters.title: Yara Hears Everything
chapters.summary: Yara tells Astrid privately that Ondrys speaks constantly through them—that the god isn't haunting Astrid but growing, using their body as soil. Astrid denies it until their reflection moves a half-second late. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: identity crisis; the question of where Astrid ends and the god begins.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Ambushed at a narrow pass by Dreven's renewed hunt, the group survives only because Astrid involuntarily channels Ondrys, fighting with impossible skill—and enjoying it. Tam witnesses and says nothing. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: exhilaration turned to shame; power's first taste of corruption.

chapters.title: Sela's True Commission
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Revealed: the free cities' council ordered her to deliver the swordspeaker alive as a living deterrent—or a sacrifice to bargain with Veyric. She hesitates, having come to respect Astrid. Emotional beat: divided loyalty; the ally is also a trap.

chapters.title: Lowmark Burns
chapters.summary: Returning to Lowmark for supplies, the company finds it razed by Veyric's purge, shrines salted, survivors branded. Yara breaks down; Astrid swears, for the first time in decades, an actual oath—to stop running. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: righteous fury; grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The God's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ondrys speaks plainly: give me your body fully and I will destroy Veyric's armies in a night. Astrid, tempted beyond anything before, nearly says yes—until Yara shows them a vision of what Ondrys's last reign cost mortals. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: the dark night of temptation; corruption offered kindly.

chapters.title: Tam's Confession
chapters.summary: Tam admits he has been reporting to Dreven under duress—his family held hostage—but he has fed false locations. Trust fractures and re-forms as the group votes to rescue his family en route. Tam's POV. Emotional beat: forgiveness tested; the found-family chooses each other deliberately.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Trap
chapters.summary: Dreven anticipated the rescue; the ambush costs Brannic his life holding the bridge. Astrid kills Dreven in single combat, refusing Ondrys's help—and winning anyway, barely. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: costly victory; proof that Astrid is enough without the god.

chapters.title: Council of Knives
chapters.summary: At the free city of Vaelport, the council demands Astrid submit to being bound as a weapon. Sela publicly breaks with them, burning her commission. Veyric's POV closes the chapter: his armies march on Vaelport within the month. Alternating POVs. Emotional beat: betrayal exposed and loyalty chosen; stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: The Siege Begins
chapters.summary: Veyric's host surrounds Vaelport. Astrid leads defenders through the sewers to burn siege engines, while Yara rallies frightened citizens to pray—not to Ondrys, but together, freely. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: solidarity under fire; ordinary courage as counter-magic.

chapters.title: Where Astrid Ends
chapters.summary: Wounded and desperate, Astrid finally lets Ondrys rise fully—and experiences total erasure inside the god's vastness, glimpsing the ancient war from the divine side. Only Yara's voice calling their true name pulls them back. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: climax of identity; Astrid learns exactly what surrender would mean.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Ondrys
chapters.summary: Climax. Before the walls of Vaelport, Astrid confronts Veyric and offers him truth instead of conquest: the gods return whether he burns shrines or not. Then, before Ondrys can seize them, Astrid uses the last of the swordspeaker rite to shatter the god-fragment in their own blood—ending the possibility of divine war forever. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: sacrificial transcendence; power refused at the ultimate cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: The gods go quiet again—but this time by choice, not suppression. Veyric, his crusade's justification gone, faces his own council's judgment. Sela and Astrid stand on Vaelport's walls, unburdened and uncertain. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: hollow peace; victory that feels like loss before it feels like freedom.

chapters.title: The Road That Chooses
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Spring in Thornfell. Astrid, no longer hiding, guides travelers openly—Sela, Tam, and Yara among them—and finds the mountain paths still shift to favor them, gently, as if the land itself remembers kindness. Astrid's POV. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; a quiet, open-ended homecoming.
